data.name: Storage Inc 2
data.detailed_description:
Notas da Atualização

Version 1.1 has been released:
-Support for Shared Screen coop has been added for up to 4 players. Requires one gamepad per player.
-Improved "Game Over" screen.


Acerca do jogo

Fun cooperative game for 1-4 players.

Each player controls a forklift truck in a warehouse.
As new goods keeps arriving, the players must work together organizing them,
so that they can make the outgoing deliveries as needed.

100 warehouse maps divided into three difficulties.
Each map have high replayability and a separate hiscore for each player count.

5 difficulty levels that controls the pace of the game, allowing you to
select something that suits you and your friends skill level and taste.
Higher difficulty increases the score for each delivery.

Your friends can join your game at any time. The game will dynamically
balance the difficulty in addition to the selected one.

How to play


Steer your truck with W, S, A, D, press Space to lift/drop and Q for horn
or with a Gamepad.
Change the controls or the reverse steering behaviour in the options.

The period bar shows the remaining time of this period.
Difficulty and player count affects the period length.
Each successfull delivery gives you score based on difficulty.

Orders indicate how many deliveries are left before the game ends.

Incoming goods arrive on conveyor belts.
If anything collides with it, a huge amount of orders will be lost.

Blue goods must be dropped in the matching delivery zone before the end of the current period.
Failure will result in a score reduction and two lost orders.

Goods with a number must be delivered during the period X periods from the current.
The number will decrease each new period.

Grey goods don't have a known delivery period, but may randomly get one each new period.

Each period, one grey goods becomes an optional bonus delivery for that period only.
It will be worth double score and may be dropped in any delivery zone.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 (or higher)
  • Processador: 1.8 GHz
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Shader Model 4 compatible
  • DirectX: Versão 11
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 70 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: DirectX compatible
  • Notas adicionais: Keyboard or Xbox 360 compatible gamepad supported. Shared Screen coop requires one gamepad per player.

reviews.review:
Here comes an honest review from someone who really digs this series. 

[h1]This game is a step down from its predecessor in nearly every single way.[/h1] 

[u]The bad[/u]:
Stacking boxes is much harder than it was in the original, thanks to the voxels, which make certain box ordering combinations from the first game impossible to pull off in this new one. Forklifts feel quite a bit different from the first game. They seem to get stuck on things more often, and seem to struggle picking up boxes at certain angles that were possible (and encouraged) in the first game. I haven't dug too far into the maps, but i'm fairly certain that a lot of these are just copies from the first game. The lack of new content in that department is quite dissappointing. Menus are not controller friendly at all (I have a wired xbox 360 controller for those interested). You cannot choose any on-screen options with the controller and must instead use a mouse. You can 'pause' the game with a controller, but that's as far as you can interact with the menu system if you're using a controller. 

Speaking of the menu system, Storage Inc. 2 has one of the worst ones I have ever used. Menus are annoying (why can i choose a map from a button on the main game screen and not by pressing 'esc' at any given point?) or straight up confusing (1] getting into the 'choose a map' screen reveals a bunch of maps that you can choose from and add strange icons to with mouse clicks? 2]  when I 'finish a map' i don't feel like I actually did. The only time the game lets you think that you beat a level is when your deliveries have been done flawlessly and you have been greeted by a string of text that says 'perfect' at the top of a menu that pops up. If you don't have a flawless game (not missing one delivery, adding every + box that pops up, never letting a delivered box blow up thanks to a new one being delivered behind it) the game presents you with a 'try again' screen for committing just one infraction. This is weirdly discouraging).

[u]The good[/u]:
The voxels look pretty nice, especially when you deliver a package and it explodes into little bits. Multiplayer is as fun as ever, and I love how anyone can play this at any skill level. The game's action is just as hectic as ever, and it is still very satisfying to create an ordered warehouse and pull off shipments quickly. I like the added + box to keep things extra tense and interesting while you sort boxes. 

[u]The verdict[/u]:
This is a step back for the series in many ways, but it's still one of the best games in the genre. For 10.99$(CAD) this isn't worth it, especially when the 360 version of the first game retails for 2.99$(CAD) and is better in every way that counts. If the price were less, or if the game were at least as good as its predecessor i'd recommend it, but until either one of these things happen I cannot recommend it.
